title: Mixed mock A: a technical screen

blocks.text: Questions on what this page has just taught. Choose one answer for each.

questions.stem: At most one of eight candidate projects on one feeder may be funded. A colleague wrote one row for each of the 28 pairs. What does replacing them by one row on the sum of all eight change?

options.text: It allows more 0/1 plans, since it drops the rows between pairs
options.says: The one row allows exactly the same 0/1 plans as the 28 pair rows.

options.text: It allows the same 0/1 plans with a tighter LP bound and fewer rows
options.says: Right: the pair rows let every project take a half in the LP; the one row does not.

options.text: It allows fewer 0/1 plans, since it also limits plans the pairs allow
options.says: Any 0/1 plan with at most one project funded satisfies both forms; the plans are the same.

options.text: It changes nothing, since the solver turns the pairs into one row
options.says: The page names two changes: a tighter LP bound and a far smaller model.

origin.section: Rapid Round: Short Answers Across Every Area

questions.stem: In a maximization, a bonus is earned only if both projects A and B are funded. You model it with a binary z whose coefficient is the bonus. Which rows must z have?

options.text: z ≤ x_A and z ≤ x_B, since the solver will push z up to earn the bonus
options.says: Right: a reward needs the rows that push z down; the third row is needed only for a cost.

options.text: z ≥ x_A + x_B − 1, since the solver will push z down to earn the bonus
options.says: A reward makes the solver push z up, so the rows that hold it down are the ones it needs.

options.text: z ≤ x_A + x_B, since one funded project is enough to earn the bonus
options.says: The bonus needs both projects; this row lets z be 1 with only one funded.

options.text: z = x_A · x_B, since HiGHS takes the product of two binaries as a row
options.says: HiGHS refuses the product itself; that is why it is replaced by linear rows.

origin.section: Rapid Round: Short Answers Across Every Area

questions.stem: A portfolio's data has a cycle in its parent links (P1 needs P2, and P2 needs P1), and the model solves with status OPTIMAL. What does that tell you about the planners' rules?

options.text: The rules are kept, since OPTIMAL proves the plan follows them
options.says: OPTIMAL is a claim about the model, not about the rules the business meant.

options.text: The data is fine, since a cycle would have made the model infeasible
options.says: The page says a cycle of parent links still solves OPTIMAL.

options.text: Not enough, since a cycle can still solve OPTIMAL; check the plan
options.says: Right: a cycle quietly drops or bundles projects; a checker that reads only the data and the plan finds it.

options.text: The cycle was reported, since the solver names rows that loop back
options.says: Nothing is reported: the page says the cycle changes the plan quietly.
